Japan AI Basic Plan re-verified and drafted as an addition. Korea: nothing new found beyond the grace-period wording.

discovery.summary: One new framework version: Meta v2.1 (2 Oct 2026, retitled Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework), with a Meta post announcing a Board AI committee. No new Anthropic RSP version (v3.4 current; policy page last updated 14 Aug 2026 with the August Risk Report), no new FSF version (v3.1), no new xAI edition (x.ai/safety still links the 30 Jun 2026 FAIF; site now branded SpaceXSI after the SpaceX acquisition), and no OpenAI Preparedness v3 found (search only; openai.com blocks automated clients). Meta's post says its update reflects 'commitments made at the White House this week'; secondary sources describe a White House accord of 29 Sep 2026 signed by six firms, but no primary text was found. The FAQ on lab frameworks was confirmed stale and a correction drafted.

discovery.area: B3 multilateral bodies and processes (L1, L5): AISR, AISI Network/NAAIMES, summits, OECD, CoE, UNESCO, UN Panel and Dialogue, plus the lost-run lead on AEF-1
discovery.summary: No new multilateral instrument meeting RUBRIC §1 found since 1 Oct 2026. (1) CoE Convention: the CoE page (Chromium) still lists the EU as the only Party. The Treaty Office chart (treaty 225) returned a Cloudflare challenge in both curl and Chromium, so the reported 15 May 2026 deposit date rests on secondary search results only. The map's 'approved Apr 2026' matches the Council approval decision of 21 Apr 2026 recorded under P-0051, so it is not wrong and no edit is proposed. (2) OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible AI (Feb 2026): the OECD page is behind Cloudflare. The Australian NCP describes it as enterprise risk-management guidance for anyone who develops or uses AI, so it is general responsible-business-conduct guidance with no frontier/GPAI-specific bearing; screened out. (3) No AISR publication after 3 Feb 2026; the UN Panel's latest output is the 21 Sep 2026 thematic brief (already on the map); no new NAAIMES output after the Jul 2026 guidance; Geneva 2027 details unchanged since Aug 2026. (4) AEF-1: drafted as a question (hold recommended).

highlights: The 2026-10-12 weekly run's research record was lost: its scheduled session could not push to GitHub. This quick partial run, requested on 13 Oct, re-checked its 28 findings from primary sources, without relying on the old wording. All held up at least in part. Several were re-drafted (Colorado now cites an Apr 27, 2026 court order in xAI v. Weiser that stays enforcement; eSafety's AI obligations come from standards made under the Act; AVERI and CAIS wording adjusted). The ledger renumbers them P-0121 to P-0149, so numbers differ from the old page.

29 proposals await your decision: 24 corrections, 1 addition (Japan AI Basic Plan, P-0124) and 4 questions with drafted options and a recommendation (AISI Network timing note P-0137, AEF-1 as an entry P-0139 with 'hold' recommended, IMDA enforceability P-0143, xAI/SpaceX note P-0131). One is new this run: the FAQ on which labs publish frontier safety frameworks is stale for OpenAI, Meta and xAI (P-0133).

Coverage: 220 sources used by earlier successful checks were re-fetched; 21 could not be (EUR-Lex 202s, several bot-blocked sites, three Chinese government sites, ilga.gov). 136 had changed bytes; 469 recorded quotations were re-tested against the new text: 453 still match, 1 matches with a new footnote marker (checked by hand), and the 15 others are explained (JavaScript-only pages, the map's own files, a reformatted API record, a page that was a 404). 38 inventory items across 22 entries were checked this run (37 changed, 1 unresolved). Everything else was not re-checked this week.

Leads not yet verified: press reports of a White House 'Accord on Super Intelligence' (29 Sep 2026) signed by six firms (no official text found); ai.gov now serves 'SI.gov' content; the EU deposit of its Council of Europe Convention ratification (15 May 2026, secondary only; the map's 'approved Apr 2026' matches the Council decision); the Australian AI Safety Institute and eSafety's 2026 AI-chatbot codes (sites unreachable).

No new answers on the review page (all 104 earlier answers were already recorded and applied). Nothing was applied, so the public map and its content date are unchanged. This run's record is pushed to branch claude/bold-dirac-97m1ik (no PR).
